{{Quote|I was expecting Lord Vader&hellip;''"<br />"''The Jedi. Where is he?''"<br />"''Oh, he's alive. For the moment. He's been in the Arena for seven days.|Baron Tarko and Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
A '''rescue mission''' to free the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] was performed in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], during the early stages of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Captured on a [[Raid on Cato Neimoidia|failed raid]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], Kota was taken to the [[City/Legends|city]] [[Tarko-se/Legends|Tarko-se]], where he was placed in the [[Tarko-se Arena]], the local [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] stadium, for [[Death/Legends|execution]]. While Kota endured an onslaught of monsters and gladiators, [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], a rogue [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of the late [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Galen Marek]], [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] from the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] on the [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]] world of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]. Unbeknownst to Kota, Vader had initiated a clandestine project to create a [[Dark Apprentice|more powerful version]] of his former [[Sith apprentice/Legends|Sith apprentice]] Marek&mdash;a perfect clone that possessed all of Marek's strengths and none of his weaknesses. However, the cloning process was imperfect and resulted in [[Aberrant clone|numerous failures]], including Starkiller.

Pursuant of information inadvertently provided by Vader, Starkiller traveled to Cato Neimoidia to rescue the captured Kota. However, his motives were more influenced by a desire to find [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], the [[Gender/Legends|woman]] with whom his progenitor had fallen in love. Starkiller fought against [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]]'s forces on his way to the arena, where he found an exhausted Kota. The desperate Tarko unleashed a beast known as the [[Gorog (creature)|Gorog]] on the two [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-wielders]], and the creature broke free of its restraints as it attempted to kill Starkiller. In the chaos, Tarko was devoured by the monster, and the arena, along with Tarko-se itself, was destroyed. Starkiller and Kota were retrieved from the falling wreckage by the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', which was on [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|The Force gives me all I need.|Starkiller, during his escape from Kamino|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
[[File:Kota_gladiator.png|thumb|left|225px|Rahm Kota fighting in the Tarko-se Arena.]]
In the early days of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="TFU2n" /> around [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]],<ref name="TFUIIComic" /> [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]] often acted without authorization from the Rebels in his military raids against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] as though he managed his [[Kota's Militia|own militia]], rather than as a part of a larger organization. During one such [[Raid on Cato Neimoidia|raid]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], Kota's [[Kota's squad|squad]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]], and he was captured. The local Imperial [[Governor/Legends|Governor]], [[Baron/Legends|Baron]] [[Merillion Tarko]], planned to [[Death/Legends|execute]] Kota by placing him in the [[Tarko-se Arena]], a [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiatorial]] arena located in the [[Bridge city/Legends|bridge]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Tarko-se/Legends|Tarko-se]]. However, Kota was able to survive for several [[Time/Legends|days]] as he fought off the monsters and gladiators sent to kill him.<ref name="TFU2n" />

Meanwhile, on the [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]] world of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] was secretly engaged in a project to recreate his slain [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]], [[Galen Marek]]&mdash;whose codename had been "Starkiller" before he became a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. The inherent difficulty with [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] resulted in [[Aberrant clone|many]] that were abject failures, either very deformed or falling prey to [[clone madness]]. At the time of a [[Sith training|training]] session, Vader informed [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]], one of the clones of Marek, of Kota's capture on Cato Neimoidia, and ordered the him to eliminate Kota at the conclusion of his training. However, the clone ultimately failed Vader's tests, unable to overcome the memory imprints from the original Marek. Before Vader could execute him, Starkiller lashed out at the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] and [[Escape from Kamino (1 BBY)|escaped]] from the facility. Starkiller hijacked [[Darth Vader's TIE Advanced/Legends|Darth Vader's TIE Advanced x1]] after fighting his way through the local Imperial [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] and escaped from the planet. With Vader's information, Starkiller traveled to Cato Neimoidia to rescue Kota, with hopes that the Jedi [[General/Legends|General]] could lead him to [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Juno Eclipse/Legends|Juno Eclipse]], who had been Marek's lover when he was alive.<ref name="TFU2n" />

==The rescue==
===Starkiller's arrival===
{{Quote|I don't know who you are, but you clearly have no idea who you are dealing with.|Baron Tarko, chiding Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
[[File:Tarko_squad.png|thumb|left|250px|Baron Tarko and his stormtroopers confront Starkiller.]]
Having not changed the [[Transponder code/Legends|transponder signal]] on the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] that he had stolen, Starkiller was identified as [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader and was directed to an executive landing platform on Cato Neimoidia. He received a full [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] [[Starfighter/Legends|fighter]] escort, was presented with a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] honor guard detail, and was greeted by Tarko himself. When Starkiller disembarked the fighter and demanded Kota's location, Tarko became suspicious and quizzed Starkiller on the local Imperial security codes. Starkiller ignited his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]], and Tarko ordered the [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] to attack before retreating himself.<ref name="TFU2n" /> Starkiller made short work of the stormtroopers, but Tarko escaped. After he destroyed a bipedal [[All Terrain Missile Platform/Legends|All Terrain Missile Platform]] [[Walker/Legends|walker]] and killed two [[Imperial Sith Acolyte]]s who stood guard at the entrance to the landing platform [[Turbolift/Legends|turbolifts]], Starkiller descended into the hanging city of Tarko-se.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

[[File:Starkiller_Cato_Neimoidia.png|thumb|right|250px|A rogue clone of the original Starkiller on Cato Neimoidia.]]
The clone Jedi initially followed the streets, all the while chided by Tarko through a loudspeaker system, but Imperial resistance&mdash;including [[Scout trooper/Legends|scout troopers]], [[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|riot stormtrooper]], and [[Jumptrooper/Legends|jumptroopers]]&mdash;prompted him to ascend to the rooftop ledges to save time. As Starkiller continued on, he used [[Mind trick/Legends|mind tricks]] to turn enemies to his side or to make them kill themselves. However, he was soon driven down by the sudden attack from a [[Nemesis-class gunship|''Nemesis''-class gunship]], and he charged into the [[Infinite Nebstar Casino]].<ref name="TFU2n" /> As most of the patrons scattered out of his way, Imperial forces flooded in. Defeating the Imperial forces in several of the rooms, Starkiller descended to the lower levels of the [[Casino/Legends|casino]] through the turbolift shafts, where he fought more Imperial resistance before he left the casino.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

Finding a [[Train/Legends|passenger tram]] to the western arch of Tarko-se, Starkiller leaped onto the vehicle's roof and used it for transport. However, the tram was attacked by Imperial air forces, including several TIE fighters and the ''Nemesis''-class [[Gunship/Legends|gunship]]. Despite Starkiller's best efforts to repel the ''Nemesis''{{'s}} own [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missiles]] back to their original source, the tram sustained heavy damage. Starkiller was nevertheless able to destroy the gunship. Due to the damage, Starkiller was forced to [[Force jump/Legends|leap]] the remaining distance to safety. Starkiller then fought his way through the rest of the Imperial forces and destroyed a second ''Nemesis''-class gunship that had joined the battle.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

===The Gorog===
{{Quote|By the Force, I knew you were alive!|Jedi General Kota, upon seeing Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2vg" />}}
Entering the Tarko-se Arena floor, Starkiller walked over to a surprised Kota. Despite being exhausted and injured after several days of combat in the arena, Kota opted to continue fighting to settle his score with Tarko. Tarko himself was desperate to defeat the resilient Starkiller, and he ordered his [[Unidentified Neimoidian aide 1|Neimoidian aide]] to release the massive arena beast known as the [[Gorog (creature)|Gorog]],<ref name="TFU2n" /> one of the largest creatures ever seen in a gladiatorial arena.<ref name="Gladiator">{{SW|url=news/galactic-gladiators-great-warriors-of-star-wars|text=Galactic Gladiators: Great Warriors of ''Star Wars''|int=Galactic Gladiators: Great Warriors of Star Wars|nolive=1}}</ref> The creature consumed a [[Bull rancor/Legends|bull rancor]] released into the arena before hauling itself out of its holding pit.<ref name="TFU2n" /> Kota departed to hunt down Tarko, leaving Starkiller to contend with the beast.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

[[File:Starkiller_v_Gorog.png|thumb|left|250px|Starkiller facing the Gorog.]]
Starkiller initially harassed the beast with [[Force lightning/Legends|Force lightning]] and [[Telekinesis/Legends|telekinetic]] attacks at its feet, but both had little effect. Following tactical advice from Kota, Starkiller used the restraint systems built into the arena to snare the Gorog's [[Limb/Legends|arms]], and leapt onto the creature's head. With a combination of lightsaber strikes and concentrated blasts of Force lightning, Starkiller was able to injure the beast. In its pain, the Gorog burst free from its restraints and swiped Starkiller off its head, sending him flying into the arena supports above. The Gorog aggressively pursued, and Starkiller got the creature to destroy the beams and cables supporting the Tarko-se Arena in an attempt to bring the whole hanging city down. He succeeded, and the structure broke apart before falling off of the Tarko-se city arch. Expecting the Gorog to fall with the arena, Starkiller headed straight for Tarko's executive box, which had its own separate support beam. Rendezvousing with Kota, the two Force-wielders made quick work of the Baron's guards before advancing on him.<ref name="TFU2vg" /><ref name="TFU2n" />

Before Starkiller and Kota could capture or kill Tarko, the Gorog grabbed hold of the box in an attempt to avoid falling, causing it to tip and dump Tarko into its mouth. The Gorog reached in and seized Kota before it lost its grip and fell. Starkiller leaped after the Gorog, using the Force to increase his velocity and dodging falling debris. He propelled himself onto the Gorog's back, from where he fired a concentrated blast of Force lightning into its torso<ref name="TFU2n" /> that stopped one of its [[Heart/Legends|hearts]].<ref name="TFUIIComic" /> The Gorog went limp and released Kota. As Kota and Starkiller fell, the Jedi General activated a remote transponder that he had concealed on his person, summoning the [[Starship/Legends|starship]] ''[[Rogue Shadow]]'', which was flying on [[Autopilot/Legends|autopilot]]. The ship swooped beneath Starkiller and Kota, allowing the pair to make it safely away.<ref name="TFU2n" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Fine, then. Go to the forests of Kashyyyk or the caves of Dagobah, or wherever you think you'll find what you need and let the galaxy die.|Rahm Kota, to Starkiller|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
Soon afterward, the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]]&mdash;who had accepted a [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] put on Starkiller's head by Vader&mdash;arrived on Cato Neimoidia with his partner, [[Xasha]]. The two entered the ruins of Tarko-se, where they found the Gorog still alive. Although the creature was seriously wounded, it attacked Fett. The bounty hunter fired a back-mounted [[Missile/Legends|rocket]] at the Gorog's second heart and used his [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] to fly through the wound in the Gorog's torso, finally killing it. The encounter with the beast discouraged Xasha from pursuing their prey any further, and she parted ways with Fett, who continued with his assignment.<ref name="TFUIIComic" />

[[File:Kota_Starkiller.png|thumb|right|250px|Jedi General Rahm Kota confronts Starkiller about his priorities.]]
Meanwhile, unaware that Marek's former ship, the ''Rogue Shadow'', was flying on autopilot, Starkiller charged into the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]], expecting to find Juno Eclipse. Kota revealed that he did not know where she was, as the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel Fleet]] had been scattered, but he did agree to provide the rendezvous coordinates with the Rebel [[Fleet/Legends|Fleet]] in the [[Athega system]]. Upon their arrival, they were ambushed by an Imperial fleet and forced to flee. Kota tried to convince Starkiller to join the Rebellion, hoping to use Starkiller's powers in a full-scale counterattack against the Empire. However, Starkiller refused to go along with Kota's plan because his sole wish was to find Eclipse. Kota disregarded Starkiller's claims of being a clone with the supposed certainty that cloning Force-sensitives was impossible, and he tried to drill Starkiller for information on the Kamino cloning facilities.<ref name="TFU2n" />

Despite Kota's claims, Starkiller remained unconvinced that he could be the real Starkiller, Galen Marek. However, he remained committed to finding Eclipse and stated that he simply needed a quiet place to [[Meditation/Legends|meditate]] on his situation. Realizing that he could not convince or force Starkiller to change his mind, Kota gave the ''Rogue Shadow'' to Starkiller, as he felt that the ship was rightfully his. Kota then demanded to be let out at the nearest [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] before Starkiller continued on his personal quest.<ref name="TFU2n" />

Starkiller dropped Kota off on the planet [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] before following up on one of the hints that Kota had inadvertently dropped, which led to the planet [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]]. Making his way through the swamps of the world, Starkiller encountered a [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]]&ndash;in&ndash;[[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]], [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], who was watching over the planet's [[Cave of Evil/Legends|Dark Side Cave]]. Yoda convinced Starkiller to enter the cave, where he experienced a [[Force vision/Legends|vision]] of Eclipse being attacked and wounded on the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of her [[Warship/Legends|warship]], the [[Salvation (flagship)|''Salvation'']]. Determined to prevent that outcome, Starkiller retrieved Kota on Malastare, and the two rendezvoused with the Rebel Fleet near the [[Itani Nebula/Legends|Itani Nebula]]. The two were too late, however; Eclipse was [[Battle near the Itani Nebula|captured]] by Boba Fett, who had been hired by Vader to bring her to Kamino in order to [[Assault on Kamino|lure]] Starkiller there.<ref name="TFU2n" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Why don't you sit this one out, General?''"<br />"''Never. I've got a score to settle.|Starkiller and Kota, in a quote from the novel|<ref name="TFU2n" />}}
The rescue of Rahm Kota first appeared in author [[Sean Williams]]'s [[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|novelization]] of the ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]]; the novel was published on [[October 5]], [[2010]].<ref name="TFU2n" /> An opportunity to play through the mission was presented in one of the levels of the video game, which itself came out on [[October 26]], 2010. The [[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] version of the game follows the novel's basic storyline, but differs from the [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions in the city layout and gameplay. Since the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 versions stay closer to the book than the Wii version, this article has been written according to their versions. The Cato Neimoidia portion of the Wii version takes place over two missions, ''City of Bridges'' and ''Baron Tarko's Palace.'' The intro to the first mission is identical to the Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 version. The scene from the novel is slightly different from the one in the game. The dialogue is adjusted and when Starkiller arrives, he finds Kota facing a stormtrooper, not gladiators.<ref name="TFU2vg" />

[[File:Gorog_wii.jpg|thumb|left|200px|The Gorog in the Wii version, without a head covering.]]
After the intro, Starkiller arrives and fights through Tarko's first line of stormtroopers, which is led by a [[Stormtrooper Commander/Legends|stormtrooper commander]]. Imperial riot stormtroopers then arrive. After dispatching the Imperials, Starkiller steps onto the elevator to rise to the next level, where he faces more stormtroopers. Starkiller chases the Baron, who has escaped across a retractable bridge. Starkiller uses the Force to re-extend the bridge, and then fights through the next bridge. However, the Baron escapes onto a passenger tram. The nearby door opens into Tarko-se and Starkiller is met by riot stormtroopers. Starkiller throws his lightsabers at a panel on the far wall, which unlocks it and drops the door, turning it into a platform. Starkiller gets on it and then uses saber throw again on the next platform, which he jumps onto to gain access to the far platform. At that point, Starkiller is ambushed by jumptroopers. After defeating them, Starkiller Force jumps across the next platforms, and uses the Force to extend another bridge.<ref name="wii">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'' ([[Wikipedia:Wii|Wii]] version)</ref>

Once in the city, Starkiller fights through more stormtroopers and reaches a bridge which is protected by the city's defense turrets. The turrets destroy the bridge while Starkiller dashes across. In the next room, Starkiller Force jumps across three platforms. Once outside, Starkiller is met by reinforcements from a dropship. Starkiller crosses another bridge while a defense turret fires on him. Once across, Starkiller turns to the left and Force-jumps up three columns to the next part of the city and uses the Force to bring down another dropship. He then crosses another bridge, which was also destroyed by a laser turret, and turns to the left. He blows apart a door with a Force push and faces more Imperial troops, and then enters another elevator. On the next level, he destroys a large turret and the resulting explosion blows him down to the casino level.<ref name="wii" />

In front of the casino, Starkiller dispatchs a carbonite war droid, and then uses his Force powers to unlock the door. Inside, Starkiller fights through more stormtroopers. He then takes an eleveator to the next level and fights another carbonite war droid. At the end of the casino, Starkiller uses Force Repulse to blow through the roof and goes outside. He uses his Force lightning to charge an elevator and rides it to the next level, where he faces a group of [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]]. Starkiller then rides a passenger tram to the other side of the city while jumptroopers harass him. A TIE fighter blows the end of the track, and, as the tram crashes, Starkiller leaps off the tram and lands on the western edge of the city.<ref name="wii" />

Starkiller fights his way through the assembled Imperials and ascends to another level of the Baron's Palace where he duels another carbonite war droid. Continuing along the corridor, the Imperials block the entrance. Starkiller uses Force Repulse to expand a crack in the floor and falls through it. In that room, Starkiller faces more Ugnaughts and Imperial troops. Starkiller then proceeds deeper into the palace and fights two more carbonite war droids. At the end of the room, Starkiller uses the Force to unlock the door. In the next chamber, he destroys another carbonite war droid, and then rides an elevator down. Starkiller then arrives in the Tarko-se Arena, and the Baron orders the Gorog to be released. Down in the main arena, Starkiller reunites with General Kota who had just struck down two [[Unidentified Weequay gladiator|gladiators]] with his lightsaber. The duel with the Gorog proceeds similarly to the other versions, except that Starkiller does not jump onto the Gorog's head, and the Gorog grabs and eats Tarko deliberately. The Gorog also lacks the head covering seen in the other versions.<ref name="wii" />

In [[2012]], the mission was mentioned in ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'', a guide to ''[[Star Wars]]'' books. In the book, it mistakenly states that PROXY was flying the ''Rogue Shadow'' during Starkiller's escape from Cato Neimoidia with Kota;<ref name="ERC">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> ''The Force Unleashed II'' novel states that the ship was on auto-pilot.<ref name="TFU2n" /> The [[2014]] [[StarWars.com]] article "[[Galactic Gladiators: Great Warriors of Star Wars]]" innaccurately placed the rescue in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]].<ref name="Gladiator" />
